Definition: from a derivative of G1364; to make apart, i.e. sunder (figuratively, alienate):--set at variance.
BiblicalUsage: To set at variance is to divide a household against itself, and Jesus uses the word once, for the sword He brings. A man will be set at variance against his father, and a daughter against her mother, and the division is over Him.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the variance Jesus brings is the cost of following Him; he does not divide families for sport; He divides them because truth demands a choice, and the choice is the most serious thing in life.
